To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the viscosity function of an extruded rubber blend is significantly different from the one measured in a capillary rheometer.
The influence of an extruded rubber blend on the viscosity function can be identified by capillary and extrudometer tests.
the extrusion process has a strong effect on the viscosity function, and that the influence of extrudability is strongly related to the viscosity function.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following topics.
the following questions: • Is there a difference in the viscosity function of a rubber blend, measured by means of an industrial extrusion rheometer, and by means of a capillary rheometer?
the development and application of an extrusion tool for material characterization of rubber blends.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
extrusion of the rubber compound leads to an increase in the apparent shear viscosity of the rubber compound and rubber blends.
the extrusion process does not influence the viscosity function of the rubber blends.
the extrusion process leads to a significant increase of the viscosity of rubber materials.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we were able to show that the extrusion rheometer can be used for characterizing rubber compounds.
extruded rubber blends show a higher apparent viscosity than blends with the same composition but tested with a capillary rheometer.
the viscosity function of an extruded material can be identified by means of an industrial extrusion rheometer (Fig. 1).
The main takeaway from our work is that
the extrusion of rubber blends has a considerable influence on the viscosity of the material.
the extrusion rheometer can be used to characterize the rheology of rubbers and rubber blends in the same way as capillary rheometers.
the extrusion rheometer is an effective tool to determine the viscosity of extruded rubber compounds.
